questions.takeaway: AWS runs and replicates EBS, while the customer schedules, encrypts, prunes and test-restores its own snapshots.

read.text: Your part: schedule snapshots, prune them to control cost, encrypt sensitive data, verify integrity and test restores.

questions.stem: A bike rental shop runs its booking app on Amazon EC2 and protects the app's Amazon EBS volumes with snapshots. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is the shop's own?

options.text: Replicating each volume within its Availability Zone
options.why: EBS copies every volume inside its zone automatically, so this protection is handled by AWS.

options.text: Storing snapshots across several Availability Zones
options.why: Snapshots are kept in Amazon S3 with redundant copies in several zones, which AWS arranges without customer work.

options.text: Removing old snapshots to keep costs down
options.why: Pruning snapshots to control cost is part of looking after the data, which is the shop's share as the customer.

options.text: Keeping each incremental snapshot usable as a full copy
options.why: AWS manages the links between incremental snapshots, so each one restores in full without customer effort.

questions.takeaway: On-premises capacity is a fixed cost bought for the peak, while EC2 bills only for instances that are running.

read.text: Owning means upfront purchases, delivery waits, installation and fixed capacity.

questions.stem: A logistics firm buys enough on-premises servers for its busiest season, and most of them sit idle the rest of the year. Which trait of Amazon EC2 removes the cost of that off-season capacity?

options.text: Only running instances are billed, so spare ones can be stopped
options.why: The firm can stop or terminate spare instances after its busy season and pay nothing for their compute time.

options.text: A term commitment lowers the hourly rate for steady, predictable use
options.why: A term commitment suits steady use, but this load is seasonal, so the firm would keep paying in the quiet months.

options.text: AWS takes care of the physical hosts that instances run on
options.why: AWS does manage the hosts, but the firm would still pay for any instances it left running all year.

options.text: Instances can be launched in Regions near the firm's customers
options.why: Launching near customers can cut latency, but it does not stop the firm from paying for off-season capacity.

questions.takeaway: Savings Plans trade a usage commitment over a term for prices below On-Demand, the save when you commit principle.

read.text: Save when you commit: a usage commitment, usually 1 or 3 years, earns big discounts on steady workloads.

questions.stem: Savings Plans price certain AWS services, such as compute, below On-Demand rates. What does the customer give in return for that lower price?

options.text: A promise of steady usage over a set term
options.why: Savings Plans follow the save when you commit principle, trading a usage commitment over a term for a discount.

options.text: A larger total volume of monthly usage
options.why: Lower prices for more volume come from tiered pricing, which needs no commitment at all.

options.text: The right for AWS to reclaim the capacity
options.why: Capacity that AWS can reclaim describes discounted spare capacity, rather than a commitment-based plan.

options.text: Payment only for the hours a resource runs
options.why: Paying only while resources run is plain pay as you go, the On-Demand model the plan is priced against.

questions.takeaway: AWS's bulk hardware buying lowers prices for every customer, so even small startups can afford advanced technology.

read.text: AWS buys hardware in bulk for its worldwide data centers and passes the lower prices on.

questions.stem: A small startup that sells handmade candles runs on the same kind of advanced infrastructure as large enterprises, at prices it can afford. This is possible because AWS buys hardware in enormous volumes and passes the savings on. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud is this?

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.why: This benefit is about paying for use instead of upfront, while the startup's gain comes from AWS's bulk buying.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.why: Lower prices that come from AWS buying hardware in bulk for all customers are the economies of scale benefit.

options.text: Stop spending on data center upkeep
options.why: This benefit is about handing off facility upkeep, while the startup's gain is a lower price per resource.
Going global is about deploying in other countries quickly, which has nothing to do with the price paid.

questions.takeaway: AWS lists migration specialists by phase or kind of help as AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners.

read.text: The AWS Competency Partner Program lists migration partners by phase or kind of help: see AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners.

questions.stem: Who are the AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners?

options.text: Outside firms recognized by AWS for skill in given phases or needs of a move
options.why: These are AWS partners that specialize in particular migration phases or needs, listed by phase or by the kind of help.

options.text: Consultants employed by AWS itself who take on project work such as complex moves
options.why: Consultants employed by AWS describe AWS Professional Services, while these competency partners are outside firms.

options.text: Architects on the AWS staff who help customers design scalable and secure apps
options.why: That describes AWS solutions architects, who work for AWS rather than being outside firms recognized for migration skill.

options.text: Community members who answer questions on a public AWS question and answer site
options.why: That describes contributors on AWS re:Post, an open community rather than firms recognized for migration skill.

questions.takeaway: A padlock and HTTPS in the browser mean the site uses an SSL/TLS certificate for an encrypted connection.

read.text: A browser padlock and an HTTPS address signal an SSL/TLS certificate.

questions.stem: A visitor sees a padlock and an HTTPS address in the browser bar. What does that signal about the site?

options.why: The padlock and HTTPS show the site uses a certificate to prove its identity and encrypt the connection.

options.text: It stores data encrypted at rest
options.why: The browser bar says nothing about how the site stores data; the padlock is about the connection.

options.text: It requires MFA for each visitor
options.why: A padlock does not mean visitors must sign in with extra factors; it concerns the connection only.

options.text: It filters traffic through a web ACL
options.why: Web ACL filtering happens out of the visitor's view and is not what the padlock reports.

questions.takeaway: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations links many accounts to one primary account and adds discounts.

read.text: With consolidated billing, subaccounts (by team, project, department or any split) link to a primary account that alone receives the bill and sees all spend.

questions.stem: A media group keeps separate AWS accounts for its news, radio and events teams. It wants the accounts linked so their combined usage can earn discounts, with all spend visible from one primary account. What should it set up?

options.why: Consolidated billing links the team accounts to one primary account that sees all spend, and Organizations adds the discounts.

options.text: Cost allocation tags on each team's resources
options.why: Tags group costs inside an account by label, but they do not link the accounts or pool their usage.

options.text: An AWS Budgets budget in each team account
options.why: Budgets warns when spend nears a limit, but each account would stay separate with no pooled usage.

options.text: AWS Cost Explorer reports in each account
options.why: Cost Explorer charts spend inside each account, but it does not link the accounts or earn any discount.

questions.takeaway: Object storage keeps self-contained objects of data, ID and metadata, and replaces a whole object on any change.

read.text: An object holds data, a unique ID and metadata, and any change rewrites the whole object.

questions.stem: Which statements describe object storage? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Each item is kept with a unique ID and metadata
options.why: An object bundles its data with an identifier and descriptive metadata, which is how object storage keeps it.

options.text: An edit rewrites only the blocks that changed
options.why: Rewriting only changed blocks is how block storage works, while an object is replaced as a whole.

options.text: Items sit in a folder hierarchy shared over a network
options.why: A shared folder hierarchy describes file storage, while objects sit in flat buckets.

options.text: An edit replaces the whole item, not only a part
options.why: Objects are updated as complete units, which is why object storage suits files that rarely change.

options.text: A volume attaches to one instance like a drive
options.why: A volume attached like a drive describes block storage, while objects are reached in buckets, not mounted on an instance.

options.text: Many users open one file system over a network
options.why: One file system opened by many users describes file storage, while object storage keeps separate objects in buckets.

questions.takeaway: AWS Compute Optimizer points out overprovisioned instances, which is the starting point for rightsizing them.

read.text: AWS Compute Optimizer, a cost-minded sidekick, flags overprovisioned instances.

questions.stem: A property management company suspects that many of its Amazon EC2 instances are larger than their workloads need. Which service reviews how the instances are used and flags the overprovisioned ones so the company can resize them?

options.why: Compute Optimizer looks at how instances are used and flags the ones that are bigger than the work requires.
The Cost and Usage Report delivers detailed cost and usage data as files, without judging whether each instance is oversized.
Budgets warns when spend nears a limit, but it says nothing about which instances are oversized.
The Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a planned design, rather than reviewing instances already running.

questions.takeaway: Moving a large legacy estate fast with no application changes, servers becoming VMs, is the rehost strategy.

read.text: Apps move as they are, often servers turned into VMs, with no changes at first

questions.stem: A car parts distributor must move a large legacy estate to AWS quickly. Its physical servers will become virtual machines on AWS, and the applications will run unchanged at first. Which migration strategy is this?

options.why: Rehosting, or lift and shift, moves apps as they are, often turning servers into VMs, which suits a large estate that must move fast.
Replatforming adds a few cloud optimizations during the move, while this plan keeps every application unchanged.
Refactoring rewrites applications with new code, the slowest path for an estate that must move quickly.
Repurchasing swaps licensed software for a SaaS product, but the distributor keeps its own applications.

questions.takeaway: Compliance stories, whitepapers and the auditing security checklist live in the Customer Compliance Center, not in Artifact.

read.text: Stories, key answers and the audit checklist live in the Customer Compliance Center, not Artifact.

questions.stem: A risk officer at a regional bank wants case studies of regulated firms that solved governance problems on AWS, plus whitepapers and a security checklist for reviewers. Where should the officer look?

options.why: The Customer Compliance Center gathers customer stories, compliance whitepapers and the auditing security checklist in one place.
Artifact supplies AWS's audit reports and agreements, while stories and the checklist live in the Compliance Center.
Audit Manager collects evidence about a company's own controls and holds no library of stories or whitepapers.
Trusted Advisor checks an account against best practices, which is no source of compliance stories or whitepapers.

questions.takeaway: Because AWS resources scale on their own, monitoring is how a team keeps checking performance and catches problems early.

read.text: AWS services scale on their own, so you must keep checking they behave.

questions.stem: An event ticketing website runs on AWS resources that add and remove capacity on their own as ticket sales rise and fall. Why does the ticketing team still need cloud monitoring?

options.text: To confirm resources keep performing well and catch problems early
options.why: Scaling happens without the team, so monitoring is how it confirms the site stays healthy and learns of trouble before buyers do.

options.text: To show regulators that its sales practices meet the laws that apply
options.why: Proving that practices meet laws is compliance, a later step that monitoring supports but does not replace.

options.text: To review on a schedule that its access controls work as planned
options.why: A scheduled review of controls is auditing, which happens periodically rather than watching health as the site scales.

options.text: To keep unauthorized users away from the ticketing servers
options.why: Keeping out unauthorized users is the job of security controls, while monitoring watches health and performance.

questions.takeaway: Security of the cloud is AWS's share, covering physical facilities, hardware and the hypervisor isolation between customers.

read.text: AWS owns security of the cloud, including all physical security, and the customer owns security in the cloud.

questions.stem: A credit union is moving its online banking application to AWS. Which security tasks are AWS's responsibility? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Controlling physical entry to the data centers
options.why: Physical security of the facilities belongs wholly to AWS and is never shared with customers.

options.text: Applying patches to the guest operating system
options.why: The credit union applies patches to the operating system it runs, since AWS cannot sign in to it.

options.text: Keeping customers isolated at the hypervisor layer
options.why: AWS secures the hypervisor layer that separates one customer's workloads from another's.

options.text: Deciding which staff members can reach member data
options.why: Choosing who can reach its data is the credit union's own access duty in the cloud.

options.text: Maintaining the server hardware behind the services
options.why: Upkeep of the hardware that runs AWS services is part of security of the cloud, which AWS owns.

options.text: Encrypting member records before they leave the office
options.why: Encrypting data before it is sent is client-side encryption, which the credit union handles itself.

questions.takeaway: AWS Business Support+ is the minimum Support plan AWS recommends for production workloads.

read.text: AWS calls Business Support+ the minimum plan it recommends for production workloads.

questions.stem: Which AWS Support plan does AWS recommend as the minimum for production workloads?

options.why: AWS names Business Support+ as the minimum plan it recommends once workloads run in production.
Basic Support is free and offers no technical support cases, which falls short for production.
Enterprise Support suits business-critical and mission-critical work, which is above the minimum.
Unified Operations is the top plan with round-the-clock workload monitoring, far above the minimum.

questions.takeaway: The free AWS Well-Architected Tool runs question-based reviews of a workload and returns issues with suggested fixes and milestones.

read.text: You define a workload, run the review on your account and get a report of issues, each with a best-practice fix.

questions.stem: A logistics company wants a free, self-service way to answer structured design questions about one of its workloads. It wants to skip questions that are irrelevant to it, record milestones over time and receive a list of issues, each with a suggested fix. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Trusted Advisor runs automated checks on an account, but it does not walk a team through design questions about a workload.
AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations, which is not a question-based design review with milestones.
The Well-Architected Tool reviews a defined workload through questions, allows not-applicable answers, tracks milestones and reports fixes.
Cost Explorer views and forecasts spending, so it cannot run a design review of a workload.

questions.takeaway: Unknown or shifting access patterns fit S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which moves objects between tiers by itself.

read.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering: for unknown or shifting access, S3 tracks use and moves each object to its cheapest suitable tier, with no lifecycle rules to manage.

questions.stem: A genomics lab stores a large dataset in Amazon S3, and nobody can predict which files researchers will open next month. The lab wants each object kept at the lowest suitable cost without writing lifecycle rules. Which storage class fits?

options.why: Standard-IA charges for each retrieval, which hurts when some files turn out to be read often.
Intelligent-Tiering watches access and moves each object to its cheapest suitable tier with no rules to manage.
Deep Archive takes hours to return data, which suits files that are almost never read, unlike this dataset.
Standard keeps every object at the frequent-access price, even the files nobody opens for months.

questions.takeaway: Tracing requests across services to find bottlenecks and debug an app points to AWS X-Ray.

read.text: AWS X-Ray: monitors and traces requests so developers can visualize app behavior, find bottlenecks, debug faster and tune efficiency and reliability.

questions.stem: A travel booking website has a slow checkout, and each request passes through several backend services. Developers want to follow individual requests end to end and see which service is causing the delay. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: CodeBuild compiles, tests and packages code, which does nothing to follow live requests through the app.
X-Ray traces requests across the app and shows where time is spent, so developers can find the slow service.
CloudTrail records API calls made in an account for auditing, not the path and timing of user requests.
AppSync builds GraphQL APIs over data sources, and it does not trace requests to find bottlenecks.

questions.takeaway: AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid storage service that joins on-premises systems with storage in AWS.

read.text: A hybrid storage service bridging on-premises systems and AWS, giving local apps virtually unlimited cloud capacity with little or no rework.

questions.stem: AWS Storage Gateway links storage in a customer's own data center with storage in AWS. Which deployment model does this support?

options.why: A cloud-based deployment runs everything in the cloud, while the gateway keeps systems on site in use.
A purely on-premises deployment uses no AWS storage, but the gateway sends data into AWS.
Joining on-site systems with cloud storage is what a hybrid deployment means, and the gateway exists to do it.
Multi-cloud spreads work over several cloud providers, while the gateway joins one data center with AWS.

questions.takeaway: Large, steady transfers from a data center that must avoid the shared internet point to Direct Connect.

read.text: Shared links can jam, so Direct Connect gives a dedicated private line from your network to a VPC (via a Direct Connect location and a virtual private gateway), cutting costs and raising bandwidth.

questions.stem: A genomics lab moves very large datasets from its data center to AWS every day. It needs steady, high throughput on a path separate from the shared public internet. Which service fits?

options.why: Direct Connect gives the lab a dedicated private line with the bandwidth and consistency these transfers need.
A Site-to-Site VPN runs over the shared internet, so heavy daily transfers can slow down.
Client VPN connects individual remote users, not a data center moving bulk data.
PrivateLink gives a VPC private access to services, not a high-bandwidth line from a data center.

questions.takeaway: Automated vulnerability scans of EC2, containers and Lambda, ranked by severity, come from Amazon Inspector.

read.text: Automatically scans EC2, containers and Lambda for vulnerabilities and best-practice gaps, like open EC2 access or vulnerable software.

questions.stem: A game studio wants its Amazon EC2 instances and Lambda functions scanned automatically for vulnerable software, with each finding ranked by severity. Which service fits?

options.why: Inspector automatically scans EC2, containers and Lambda for vulnerabilities and ranks each finding by severity with a fix.
GuardDuty looks for threats in account and network activity rather than flaws in installed software.
Detective investigates the root cause of an issue after detection and does not scan for vulnerable software.
Macie finds sensitive data in S3 buckets, so it does not inspect instances or functions for flaws.

questions.takeaway: AWS Glue is the managed ETL service for preparing data from many sources, with a visual builder and scheduling.

read.text: Managed ETL that makes prep simpler, faster and cheaper; visual job builder, built-in scheduling, many sources and formats, code-free scripts; jobs read Catalog metadata to shape transforms

questions.stem: A regional clinic network plans to use AWS Glue to prepare patient visit records from several systems for analysis. Which capabilities will AWS Glue give the network? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A visual builder for data preparation, with scheduling built in
options.why: Glue offers a visual job builder and built-in scheduling, so the network can set up and repeat its prep jobs.

options.text: Managed extract, transform and load across many sources and formats
options.why: Glue is a managed ETL service that reads many sources and formats, which fits records spread over several systems.

options.text: Custom-configured Apache Spark, Hadoop or Hive clusters for complex jobs
options.why: Custom big data clusters on Apache frameworks are Amazon EMR, while Glue keeps preparation simple and managed.

options.text: Serverless SQL over the prepared records in Amazon S3, billed per query
options.why: Ad hoc pay-per-query SQL on S3 data is the job of Amazon Athena rather than the ETL service.

options.text: Interactive dashboards and reports over the prepared records
options.why: Self-service dashboards for business users come from Amazon Quick Sight, after the data is prepared.

questions.takeaway: NoSQL differs from relational mainly by a flexible schema, not by raw speed or size.

read.text: The core difference is flexible versus rigid schema, not speed or scaling, and NoSQL still indexes the primary key by default.

questions.stem: What mainly sets a NoSQL database apart from a relational database?

options.text: Its schema is flexible, so items can hold different attributes
options.why: The core difference is the flexible schema, which lets each item carry its own set of attributes.

options.text: It indexes the primary key of every item by default
options.why: Relational databases index their primary keys too, so this trait does not set NoSQL apart from them.

options.text: It can run on AWS as a fully managed database service
options.why: AWS also runs relational engines as managed services, so being managed is not what separates the two models.

options.text: It can return query results quickly even for very large datasets
options.why: Speed and scale are not the core difference, since a relational database can also be fast for the right workload.

questions.takeaway: Running and recovering workloads at agreed service levels, with daily to yearly routines, is the AWS CAF Operations perspective.

read.text: Enable, run, use, operate and recover workloads at the level agreed with business stakeholders; set daily to yearly routines, support business operations, define current procedures plus needed process changes and training

questions.stem: An IT support manager at a regional airline must make sure cloud workloads run and recover at the service levels agreed with the business. The manager must also set routines that range from daily checks to yearly reviews. Which AWS CAF perspective guides this work?

options.why: Operations enables, runs and recovers workloads at the level agreed with the business and sets daily to yearly routines.
The Platform perspective designs architecture and the target state, before workloads are running day to day.
Governance aligns IT with business strategy and measures investments, rather than running workloads at agreed levels.
People leads change management and staffing, rather than setting the routines that keep workloads running.

questions.takeaway: AWS Health reports service events, planned changes and account notices that affect your resources.

read.text: AWS Health is the main feed of events affecting your resources.

questions.stem: Which kinds of information does AWS Health provide about the resources in an AWS account? (Select TWO.)

options.text: CPU use measured on each running instance
options.why: Performance numbers such as CPU use are CloudWatch metrics, while AWS Health reports events that AWS raises.

options.text: An inventory that lists every resource
options.why: A resource inventory comes from AWS Config, while AWS Health reports events about resources rather than listing them.

options.text: Disruptions in AWS services the account uses
options.why: AWS Health is the main feed of events that hit an account's resources, including service events such as disruptions.

options.text: Log files gathered from running applications
options.why: Collecting and searching application log files is the job of CloudWatch Logs, not of AWS Health.

options.text: Planned changes such as upcoming maintenance
options.why: AWS Health covers planned changes that will touch the account's resources, so teams can prepare for them.

options.text: A history of setting changes on resources
options.why: A history of configuration changes comes from AWS Config, while AWS Health reports AWS events and notices.

questions.takeaway: A member account can sit in an OU or directly under the root, and its charges roll up to the management account.

read.text: In an OU, or under the root and still billed jointly

questions.stem: Which statement about a member account in AWS Organizations is true?

options.text: It can sit directly under the root and still share the bill
options.why: A member account may live under the root instead of in an OU, and it is still billed through the management account.

options.text: It must first belong to an organizational unit to join at all
options.why: Placing an account in an OU is optional, since a member account may also sit directly under the root.

options.text: It gets a bill of its own apart from the organization
options.why: Member account charges roll up to the management account, so the member pays no separate bill of its own.

options.text: It creates the organization and holds final control
options.why: Creating and governing the organization is the role of the management account, the owner, rather than a member.

questions.takeaway: Serverless compute hands server provisioning and scaling to AWS while the customer keeps its code and data duties.

read.text: The servers hosting your app are hidden and out of reach.

questions.stem: A veterinary practice moves its appointment reminder app from Amazon EC2 instances it manages itself to serverless compute. Which task moves from the practice to AWS because of this change?

options.text: Provisioning and scaling the servers that run the code
options.why: On EC2 the practice sized and scaled its instances, and with serverless compute AWS provisions and scales the hidden servers.

options.text: Guarding the data centers where the servers are housed
options.why: AWS already secured the facilities while the app ran on EC2, so this task does not move with the change.

options.text: Writing and securing the reminder app's own code
options.why: The app's code and its security stay with the practice under serverless compute as well.

options.text: Deciding which staff accounts may change the app
options.why: Who may change the app is an access choice that the practice still makes after the move.

questions.takeaway: US government agencies and their contractors that need stricter facility and staff controls run in AWS GovCloud Regions.

read.text: AWS GovCloud Regions carry strict physical, operational and personnel controls for US government bodies and contractors.

questions.stem: A US federal agency and the outside contractors that run its systems need to host sensitive workloads under stricter physical, operational and staffing controls than standard AWS locations apply. Which AWS offering fits?

options.why: Outposts runs AWS services in the agency's own building, leaving the stricter staffing and operational controls it needs to the agency.
A Dedicated Host gives one customer a whole physical server, but it does not add stricter controls over the people and sites behind it.
These Regions serve US federal and other public bodies and their contractors, with stricter physical, operational and personnel controls.
Artifact hands out compliance reports and agreements; it does not host the agency's sensitive workloads anywhere.

questions.takeaway: Switching off applications that are no longer needed is the retire strategy, which saves cost and effort.

read.text: Unneeded apps are switched off

questions.stem: Which migration strategy switches off applications that an organization no longer needs, saving cost and effort?

options.why: Retire shuts down applications that are no longer needed, which saves cost and effort.
Retain keeps applications running in their current environment for now, rather than shutting them down.
Repurchase replaces an application with a SaaS product, so the work it does continues.
Relocate moves existing VMs or containers to a cloud host, so the applications keep running.

questions.takeaway: Sharing the host's OS makes containers lighter and quicker to start than full virtual machines.

read.text: Containers share the host's OS, so they are lighter, start faster and use resources better.

questions.stem: A media startup needs new copies of its service to come up quickly when traffic jumps, and it is weighing containers against virtual machines. Which statements explain why containers suit this need? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Containers share the operating system of the host machine they run on
options.why: With no OS of their own to boot, new containers come up sooner than virtual machines, which suits sudden traffic jumps.

options.text: Containers are lighter because they leave out a full operating system
options.why: A lighter unit is quicker to start, while a virtual machine must first boot its full OS on a hypervisor.

options.text: Containers bundle code and dependencies so they run the same anywhere
options.why: Portability across environments is true of containers, but it does not make new copies come up any faster.

options.text: Containers each boot a full operating system on top of a hypervisor
options.why: Booting a full OS on a hypervisor describes a virtual machine, and it is what makes new copies slower to start.

options.text: Container images sit in a registry such as Amazon ECR for later pulls
options.why: ECR does hold container images, but where images are kept does not explain why containers start sooner than VMs.

questions.takeaway: Blocking web requests from listed IP addresses through a web ACL is the job of AWS WAF.

read.text: AWS WAF: a web application firewall that refuses requests from IP addresses blocked in its web ACL (web access control list).

questions.stem: An online toy store keeps a list of IP addresses that abused its checkout and wants web requests from them refused before they reach the app. Which service fits?

options.why: AWS WAF refuses web requests from IP addresses listed as blocked in its web ACL.
Shield Advanced counters sophisticated DDoS attacks but does not keep a custom list of blocked web clients.
Firewall Manager rolls firewall rules out across many accounts; the request filtering itself is done by another service.
GuardDuty detects threats in account and network activity and does not block web requests by itself.

questions.takeaway: Text that must be heard as lifelike speech points to Amazon Polly, while speech that must become text points to Transcribe.

read.text: Assistants, e-learning, visually impaired users, studio-free narration

questions.stem: A publisher of workplace training manuals wants its readers to be able to listen to each guide read aloud in a natural voice. It wants to avoid hiring narrators for every new edition. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Polly converts written text into lifelike speech, so each new edition can be voiced without a narrator.
Transcribe works the other way round, turning recorded speech into text, while the publisher starts from text.
Translate changes text from one language to another but produces no spoken audio for listeners.
Lex builds two-way chat and voice bots, which is more than reading a fixed guide aloud.

questions.takeaway: Fully managed services shrink a customer's infrastructure work, and its cost, down to its own code.

read.text: Fully managed, like serverless Lambda: there are no servers for you to provision or manage, and AWS also covers scaling and availability.

questions.stem: Which service model removes the most infrastructure labor from a company's operating costs, leaving its staff to look after only the application code and its security?

options.why: AWS provisions, scales and runs every server, so the only work left in-house is the code and its security.
AWS runs these day to day, but some provisioning or configuration can still fall to the company's staff.
The company still patches, scales and secures each instance, so the infrastructure labor stays on its books.
Owning the hardware keeps every layer of infrastructure work, and its cost, with the company.

questions.takeaway: Creating, controlling and temporarily disabling encryption keys is the job of AWS KMS.

read.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS): creates and controls cryptographic keys, the random digit strings that lock and unlock data.

questions.stem: A law firm wants to generate the cryptographic material that locks and unlocks its case files, decide which IAM roles may use it, and switch it off for a while during an audit. Which service fits?

options.why: AWS KMS creates and controls cryptographic keys, lets the firm set who may use them, and can disable a key temporarily.
ACM manages SSL/TLS certificates for connections, not general-purpose keys that encrypt stored files.
Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets such as passwords and API keys rather than creating encryption keys.
IAM decides which identities may act in the account, but it does not generate or hold the keys that lock the files.

questions.takeaway: When the questions are about chains of relationships, such as fraud rings, a graph database like Neptune fits.

read.text: A fully managed graph database for highly connected data, like social webs that are clumsy in relational tables.

questions.stem: A payments startup wants to spot fraud rings in real time by following chains of links between accounts, devices and cards. Which database service is designed for this kind of highly connected data?

options.why: Neptune is a graph database that follows relationships quickly, which suits fraud detection across linked records.
DynamoDB looks items up by key and has no built-in way to traverse chains of relationships.
Aurora keeps data in relational tables, where many-hop relationship chains become clumsy and slow to query.
Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not a database built to traverse connected records in real time.

questions.takeaway: An SCP attached to an OU caps what users and roles in its accounts can do, whatever their IAM permissions allow.

read.text: Cap on services, resources and API actions for an account's users and roles

questions.stem: A media company wants no user or role in its development accounts to use services outside an approved list, whatever IAM permissions they hold. The development accounts sit in one OU in AWS Organizations. What should the company attach to that OU?

options.why: An SCP caps the services and actions available to users and roles in every account of the OU, whatever IAM grants them.
A managed policy is an IAM policy for users, groups or roles, and it cannot be attached to an OU.
A role is an identity that grants permissions when assumed, rather than a cap that applies across an OU's accounts.
A Config rule reports resource settings that break a rule, but it does not limit which services users can call.

questions.takeaway: Amazon EBS gives EC2 persistent block volumes whose data outlives instance stops and terminations.

read.text: They live apart from the host on durable SSD or HDD media, so data survives stops, starts and terminations.

questions.stem: Which AWS service provides block storage volumes for Amazon EC2 instances that keep their data after the instance stops or terminates?

options.why: Instance store is block storage on the host, and its data is erased when the instance stops or terminates.
EFS is a shared file system for many instances, and it does not attach as a block volume.
EBS volumes live apart from the host, so their data survives stops, starts and terminations.
S3 stores whole objects in buckets, and it does not attach to an instance as a block volume.

questions.takeaway: Moving VMs or containers that already run on premises to a cloud host is the relocate strategy.

read.text: VMs or containers already running on premises move to a cloud host

questions.stem: A software testing firm already runs all its workloads as virtual machines and containers on an on-premises virtualization platform. It wants those same virtual machines and containers to run on a cloud host instead, with no servers converted along the way. Which migration strategy fits?

options.why: Relocate takes VMs or containers that already run on premises onto a cloud host, which matches the firm's existing workloads.
Rehost lifts applications as they are, often turning servers into VMs, while this firm's workloads are already VMs and containers.
Replatform adds a few cloud optimizations to an application, while the firm only wants its existing VMs and containers on a cloud host.
Refactor rebuilds applications with new code and cloud-built features, while the firm keeps its existing VMs and containers.

questions.takeaway: Least-privilege access and encryption of data at rest and in transit are the clearest cues for the Security pillar.

read.text: Security: protection built in, with least-privilege access, intact data and guarded systems.

questions.stem: A credit union is checking its online banking design against the Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Which practices belong to that pillar? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Give each staff role only the permissions its work requires.
options.why: Least-privilege access is a central Security practice, because it limits what any one identity can reach.

options.text: Spread the database across several Availability Zones with automatic recovery.
options.why: Multiple Availability Zones and automatic recovery point to Reliability, which plans for failures.

options.text: Encrypt member data both while stored and while it travels.
options.why: Encrypting data at rest and in transit protects it from exposure, which is what the Security pillar asks for.

options.text: Resize servers so their memory matches what the workload needs.
options.why: Matching server size to the workload is Performance Efficiency, which is about fit rather than protection.

options.text: Send every release through an automated deployment pipeline.
options.why: Automated releases are an Operational Excellence practice, aimed at running systems well rather than guarding them.

questions.takeaway: AWS Config automated remediation returns noncompliant resources to the required settings without manual work.

read.text: It alerts you to noncompliant resources and can fix them automatically.

questions.stem: A school district's routine compliance scans sometimes find resources whose settings break district policy. The district wants those resources put back to the required settings without waiting for an engineer to act. Which approach fits?

options.why: Config can fix a noncompliant resource automatically, which restores the required settings with no engineer involved.

options.text: A CloudTrail trail that logs the change
options.why: A trail records who made the change, but logging it leaves the resource in its noncompliant state.

options.text: Read-only access in AWS Audit Manager
options.why: Read-only access protects audit evidence from edits, which is the opposite of changing the resource back.

options.text: A report from AWS Artifact Reports
options.why: An Artifact report describes how AWS was audited and cannot change any setting in the district's account.

questions.takeaway: AWS Security Center is the name for the cloud security site at aws.amazon.com/security.

read.text: AWS Security Center is the name AWS documentation gives the cloud security site at aws.amazon.com/security, where it points you for more on AWS security and compliance.

questions.stem: Which name does AWS documentation use for the main site it points readers to for cloud security and compliance, found at aws.amazon.com/security?

options.why: AWS Security Center is the name AWS documentation uses for that site, where it sends readers for security and compliance.
Customer Compliance Center holds customer stories, whitepapers and checklists, not the main AWS security site.
The Security Blog publishes expert tip articles at its own blog address rather than serving as the main security site.
Security Documentation holds per-product guidance at its own docs address, so it is not the main security site.

questions.takeaway: Steady, uninterrupted use in one instance family and Region, with no need for server control, fits Reserved Instances.

read.text: Reserved Instances (RIs): discounts for a 1- or 3-year term in one family and Region.

questions.stem: A toy maker runs a steady, predictable workload on one Amazon EC2 instance family in one Region and has no plans to change either for years. The workload must never be interrupted, and the toy maker needs no control over which physical server it runs on. It wants a discount in exchange for a term commitment tied to that family and Region. Which pricing option fits?

options.why: Reserved Instances give a discount for a term commitment in one family and Region, which suits steady use that will not change.
Dedicated Hosts give a whole server and control over placement, which the toy maker does not need, at a higher price than RIs.
On-Demand has no commitment and no discount, so it costs the most for a steady, predictable workload.
Spot capacity can be reclaimed by AWS, which breaks the need for a workload that must never be interrupted.

questions.takeaway: To hire an outside firm that builds solutions on AWS, a customer looks to the AWS Partner Network.

read.text: A global community of tech and consulting firms building customer solutions with AWS, solving problems and adding value.

questions.stem: A travel agency wants to hire an outside consulting firm with AWS experience to build a recommendation feature for its booking site. Where should it look for such a firm?

options.why: The Partner Network is a global community of technology and consulting firms that customers can hire to build on AWS.
re:Post lets the agency ask the community questions, but it is no directory of firms to hire for a build.
The Knowledge Center holds FAQ articles and videos, rather than consulting firms that take on projects.
The Health Dashboard reports service health for the agency's resources and lists no outside firms.

questions.takeaway: When staff need a full, persistent desktop reachable from anywhere, Amazon WorkSpaces fits rather than app streaming or a secure browser.

read.text: Amazon WorkSpaces: fully managed virtual desktop infrastructure, a complete persistent desktop staff reach securely from anywhere and use like an office PC, cost-efficient and easy to run.

questions.stem: An architecture firm has staff who work from home and from client sites. Each person needs a complete desktop that keeps their files and settings between sessions and works like an office computer. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: AppStream 2.0 streams individual applications to a browser, not a complete persistent desktop for each person.
WorkSpaces delivers a fully managed, persistent desktop that staff reach securely from anywhere like an office PC.
Secure Browser is a managed browser for web-only work, so it does not give staff a full desktop.
Lightsail offers simple virtual servers for hosting, not managed desktops for staff to work in.

questions.takeaway: A workload limited by processor speed, such as a game server, fits compute optimized instances.

read.text: Compute optimized: CPU-heavy work like game servers, HPC, machine learning and scientific modeling.

questions.stem: A game studio hosts multiplayer matches on servers that are held back by processor speed rather than by memory or disk. Which Amazon EC2 instance family fits best?

options.why: Compute optimized instances are built for CPU-heavy work such as game servers.
General purpose instances balance resources, so they give less CPU per dollar than this workload needs.
Memory optimized instances help with large in-memory datasets, but memory is not the limit here.
Accelerated computing adds GPUs and co-processors, which a CPU-bound game server does not need.

questions.takeaway: To search an application's own log files in one place, use CloudWatch Logs rather than CloudTrail's API records.

read.text: Collect, store and monitor log files centrally; view, search, filter

questions.stem: Players of a game studio's online title reported failed sign-ins last night. The engineers want the error messages that the game server's application writes collected in one place, so they can search them. Which service fits?

options.why: CloudWatch Logs collects application log files centrally and lets the engineers search and filter them for the errors.
Event history lists API and console calls made in the account, while the sign-in errors live inside the game's own logs.
Config records and judges resource settings, which would show no application error messages from the game server.
Trusted Advisor checks the account against best practices, and it does not read or search an application's log files.

questions.takeaway: Amazon Q Developer serves programmers with code suggestions, while Q Business serves other staff.

read.text: Suggests code, even whole functions and logical blocks, in multiple IDEs; languages include C#, Java, JavaScript, Python, TypeScript

questions.stem: Which AWS service acts as a generative AI coding assistant that proposes code, up to complete functions, inside the editors programmers already use?

options.why: Q Developer is the coding assistant that suggests code blocks and functions in many popular IDEs.
Q Business helps employees with questions and tasks drawn from company data, not with writing code.
Bedrock gives developers access to foundation models to build their own apps, not a ready coding assistant.
JumpStart is a hub of models to fine-tune and deploy, not an assistant that writes code in an editor.

questions.takeaway: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling gives elasticity, so capacity follows unpredictable demand and only running instances are paid for.

read.text: A new store cannot predict its traffic spikes: let Auto Scaling follow demand.

questions.stem: A newly opened pet supply retailer cannot predict when traffic to its online store will spike. It turns on Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling for the instances behind the store. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud does this give the retailer?

options.text: Its capacity follows demand, so it pays only for what it needs
options.why: Auto Scaling adds instances as traffic rises and removes them as it falls, which is elasticity with no forecast needed.

options.text: Its requests are spread evenly over the instances already running
options.why: Spreading requests over running instances is the job of Elastic Load Balancing, not of Auto Scaling.

options.text: Its hourly compute rate drops in return for a long-term commitment
options.why: A lower rate for a commitment comes from a pricing option such as Savings Plans, not from Auto Scaling.

options.text: Its store can reach shoppers abroad from Regions close to them
options.why: Serving shoppers from nearby Regions is global reach, which Auto Scaling does not provide.

questions.takeaway: Control Tower controls, or guardrails, block nonconforming deployments and catch noncompliant accounts and resources.

read.text: Controls (guardrails): high-level rules, like road crash barriers, that block nonconforming deployments and catch and fix noncompliant accounts and resources.

questions.stem: A toy manufacturer governs its accounts with AWS Control Tower. It wants high-level rules that stop teams from deploying resources that break company policy and that catch accounts already out of line. Which part of Control Tower provides these rules?

options.why: Guardrails, also called controls, are high-level rules that block nonconforming deployments and detect noncompliant accounts and resources.
Account Factory creates new accounts from a template, but it does not police resources after they are deployed.
The landing zone marks what falls under the rules, while the rules themselves come from the controls.
The dashboard shows compliance status, so it reports on problems without blocking any deployment.

questions.takeaway: Static IPs plus fast, health-aware failover across Regions on the AWS network point to Global Accelerator.

read.text: Global Accelerator moves app traffic off crowded public routes onto the AWS private global network for better availability, performance and security.

questions.stem: A ride-hailing company runs its booking API in more than one AWS Region for riders around the world. It wants rider traffic sent to fixed IP addresses and carried on the AWS private backbone, and moved quickly to a healthy Region if one fails. Which service fits?

options.why: Global Accelerator gives static IP addresses and steers traffic over the AWS network to healthy endpoints with fast failover.
CloudFront caches content at edge locations, but the need here is fast failover of live API traffic between Regions.
Route 53 answers DNS lookups, but it does not give the API fixed IP addresses or carry traffic on the AWS backbone.
Transit Gateway links VPCs and on-premises networks as a hub, not riders on the internet to the closest healthy Region.

questions.takeaway: Avoiding upfront hardware spend and coping with unknown demand point to the variable expense and stop guessing capacity benefits.

read.text: On AWS, spending follows usage and capacity follows demand.

questions.stem: A meal-kit delivery startup wants to avoid a large upfront hardware purchase, and it has no reliable way to tell how many orders it will get next year. Which benefits of the AWS Cloud address these two concerns? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.why: Paying each month for what is used, instead of buying hardware upfront, is the trade fixed expense for variable expense benefit.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.why: Economies of scale lower unit prices through bulk buying, which neither removes the upfront purchase nor answers the unknown order volume.
Provisioning for today and scaling with real demand means the startup need not predict next year's order volume.
Speed and agility is about quick, disposable test environments, which addresses neither the upfront purchase nor the unknown demand.
Going global is about deploying near users in other countries, which touches neither the upfront cost nor the order forecast.

questions.takeaway: Keeping a business-critical app where it is for now, such as one that needs major refactoring, is the retain strategy.

read.text: Business-critical apps stay in the source environment for now: those needing major refactoring, work that can wait, or apps months from deprecation

questions.stem: A freight broker has a business-critical billing application that would need major refactoring before it could run on AWS. The broker decides to keep it in its current data center for now and revisit it later. Which migration strategy is this?

options.why: Retain keeps business-critical applications that need major refactoring in the source environment for now.
Retire switches an application off, while this billing application stays in use.
Rehost would move the application to AWS unchanged, while the broker keeps it on premises for now.
Relocate moves existing VMs or containers to a cloud host, while the broker moves nothing yet.

questions.takeaway: Work that wants GPUs or other hardware accelerators, such as rendering, fits accelerated computing instances.

read.text: Accelerated computing: hardware accelerators such as GPUs, co-processors that do floating-point math, graphics, pattern matching and machine learning more efficiently than software running on a CPU.

questions.stem: A film studio renders visual effects and wants GPUs to handle the graphics math faster than software on a CPU could. Which Amazon EC2 instance family fits?

options.why: Accelerated computing instances carry GPUs that do graphics math more efficiently than CPU-run software.
Compute optimized instances add CPU power, but the studio wants GPUs instead of faster CPUs.
Memory optimized instances help with large in-memory datasets, not with GPU graphics work.
General purpose instances balance resources and do not provide the GPUs rendering needs.

questions.takeaway: An EU business that must get consent and let people view or erase their personal data is meeting GDPR.

read.text: Under GDPR, the EU privacy law, an EU online shop must get consent before collecting personal data and let people see or erase it.

questions.stem: An online pharmacy based in Spain takes card payments from shoppers across the European Union and keeps their names, emails and order history. It must get each shopper's permission before collecting these details and let shoppers view or erase them on request. Which rules set these duties?

options.why: HIPAA is a US law on health information, so it does not set consent and erasure duties for a pharmacy serving EU shoppers.
PCI rules protect the card data the pharmacy takes at checkout, but they do not cover consent or erasing personal details.
GDPR is the EU privacy law that requires consent before collecting personal details and lets people see or erase them.
These rules decide where data must be stored, not consent or a shopper's right to view and erase their details.

questions.takeaway: Storing and rotating passwords, database credentials and API keys centrally points to AWS Secrets Manager.

read.text: AWS Secrets Manager is the central place to store, fetch and rotate secrets such as passwords, database credentials and API keys.

questions.stem: A ski resort's booking app reads a database password that is hardcoded in its source, and the team wants it stored centrally and rotated on a schedule. Which service fits?

options.why: Secrets Manager is the central place to store, fetch and rotate secrets such as database credentials.
AWS KMS creates and controls encryption keys, but it does not store and rotate an app's database password.
ACM manages SSL/TLS certificates for connections, not passwords that an app uses to reach a database.
Systems Manager oversees and patches nodes, and it is not the service built to rotate a database password on a schedule.

questions.takeaway: Protect the root user with a strong password and MFA, since policies, groups and password policies never restrict it.

read.text: Give it a strong password and turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) right after the first root login.

questions.stem: A furniture maker has just opened a new AWS account and signed in as the root user for the first time. Which steps protect that root user, as AWS advises? (Select TWO.)

options.why: AWS advises a strong password on the root user, since that identity can do anything in the account.

options.text: Turn on MFA for its sign-in
options.why: Turning on MFA right after the first sign-in adds a second proof the root user must present.
Password policies set rules for IAM user passwords, but they never apply to the root user's password.
The root user can do anything and cannot be restricted, so an attached policy would not protect or limit it.

options.text: Add it to a restricted IAM group
options.why: Groups pass their permissions to IAM users, and the root user cannot be restricted that way, so this protects nothing.

questions.takeaway: Repeated, scripted launches from typed commands point to the AWS CLI rather than the console or an SDK.

read.text: The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) issues API calls as text commands on Windows, macOS or Linux, so repetitive work can be scripted, and automation keeps deployments predictable.

questions.stem: A news website's operations team launches the same set of servers several times a week. It wants each launch to be predictable and written as text instructions that it can save, rerun and automate, without writing application code. Which tool fits?

options.why: The AWS CLI issues API calls as typed instructions that can be scripted, which keeps repeated launches predictable.
Clicking through the console for every launch is slow and easy to get wrong, and it is not scriptable.
An SDK calls AWS from application code, which the team wants to avoid writing.
Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations and does not launch servers from commands.

questions.takeaway: In the migrate and modernize phase each app is moved and validated, with tools such as AWS Application Migration Service.

read.text: Migrate and modernize: architect, migrate and validate each app, alone or with specialists and competency partners.

questions.stem: A bike rental chain has an approved migration plan and now begins moving each application to AWS and checking that it works there. Which service is built for this phase?

options.why: Application Migration Service is a last-phase tool that replicates applications to AWS, which fits migrate and modernize.
Migration Evaluator builds the business case in the assess phase, which the chain has already passed.
Application Discovery Service inventories servers to inform the plan in the mobilize phase, before applications move.
The Pricing Calculator estimates AWS costs during planning and moves no applications.

questions.takeaway: Encrypted links from offices to a VPC without a dedicated line call for Site-to-Site VPN.

read.text: For sites: encrypted links from data centers or branch offices to your VPC, with high availability, private sessions and faster apps.

questions.stem: A furniture retailer wants its branch offices joined to its VPC through encrypted tunnels over the internet. The links carry modest traffic, so a shared internet path is good enough. Which service fits?

options.why: Site-to-Site VPN builds encrypted links from offices to a VPC over the internet without a dedicated line.
Direct Connect is a dedicated line, which the retailer does not need for modest office traffic.
Client VPN connects individual remote users rather than whole branch office networks.
Transit Gateway is a hub that joins networks, but it is not the encrypted office link itself.

questions.takeaway: S3 durability comes from automatic redundant copies across several Availability Zones in the chosen Region.

read.text: For most storage classes AWS keeps redundant copies automatically, giving 11 nines (99.999999999 percent) of durability, so losing an object within a year is vanishingly unlikely.

questions.stem: Most Amazon S3 storage classes are designed for 11 nines of durability. Which trait of Amazon S3 is the source of that durability?

options.text: S3 encrypts objects at rest and in transit to keep them confidential
options.why: Encryption keeps data private, but it does not protect an object from being lost.

options.text: S3 keeps copies of each object in several Availability Zones
options.why: S3 automatically keeps redundant copies across several zones of the Region, which makes losing an object very unlikely.

options.text: S3 Lifecycle can move objects to cheaper storage classes
options.why: Lifecycle rules lower storage cost as data ages, and they play no part in keeping objects intact.

options.text: S3 scales a bucket's storage with no fixed ceiling
options.why: Unlimited room lets a bucket keep growing, but how much it can hold says nothing about how safely each object is kept.

questions.takeaway: Aurora suits replacing costly commercial relational engines, matching their performance for much less.

read.text: About one-tenth the cost of high-end commercial databases at similar performance, so it suits replacing pricey commercial engines.

questions.stem: An insurance broker pays steep license fees for a high-end commercial relational database. It wants a managed, MySQL-compatible database that gives similar performance for far less money. Which service fits?

options.why: Aurora is MySQL-compatible and delivers commercial-grade performance at a small fraction of the cost.
DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value database, so it is not a MySQL-compatible stand-in for a relational engine.
Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics rather than a replacement for an operational relational database.
Neptune is a graph database for highly connected data and does not offer MySQL compatibility.

questions.takeaway: AWS Batch schedules and scales large parallel jobs that are too heavy for event-driven functions.

read.text: It schedules jobs and scales resources to fit them across a fleet such as EC2 instances.

questions.stem: A university genomics lab must run a large number of parallel analysis jobs, many of which take hours each. It wants AWS to schedule the jobs and scale a fleet of instances to fit the work. Which service fits?

options.why: AWS Batch schedules jobs and scales compute across instances, which suits long, parallel genomics work.
Lambda runs short, event-driven tasks, and its run time cap is too brief for hours-long jobs.
Lightsail sells fixed server bundles for small sites, and it does not schedule or scale a job fleet.
Elastic Beanstalk deploys and scales web apps, not queues of heavy compute jobs.

questions.takeaway: Only a multi-Region design keeps a workload running when an entire Region goes down.

read.text: Multi-Region goes one step further and survives a whole Region going down.

questions.stem: Which deployment design keeps a workload available even when every Availability Zone in its home Region becomes unreachable?

options.text: Running copies in more than one Region
options.why: Copies in another Region keep serving when the whole home Region is down, which is the failure the stem describes.

options.text: Running copies in several AZs of one Region
options.why: Several AZs in one Region protect against a single AZ failing, not against all of that Region's AZs failing together.
Edge locations cache content for speed and are not built to run the workload or its databases.
Auto Scaling adds capacity inside the Region, so the new instances fail along with the Region.

questions.takeaway: Multi-petabyte moves from sites without internet point to Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices, which ship data offline.

read.text: AWS Snow Family devices with NVMe storage for multi-petabyte moves from on-premises sites where internet may be unavailable.

questions.stem: An oil exploration company must move multiple petabytes from a remote field site with no internet access into AWS. What should it do?

options.text: Ship the data to AWS on Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices
options.why: Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices carry multi-petabyte moves offline from sites where internet may be unavailable.

options.text: Install an AWS Outposts rack on premises to hold the data
options.why: Outposts runs AWS infrastructure on premises and needs a network link back to its Region, which this field site lacks.

options.text: Run AWS DataSync tasks that copy the data into Amazon S3 each night
options.why: DataSync moves data over the network, which this field site lacks.

options.text: Mount an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises and write the data to it
options.why: An S3 File Gateway stores files in Amazon S3 over the network, so it needs the internet access this site lacks.

questions.takeaway: Deploying into an existing AWS Region in a new country, rather than building facilities, is the go global in minutes benefit.

read.text: A US company expanding to India can deploy to an AWS-managed Region there instead of building its own data centers, in minutes rather than months or years.

questions.stem: A language-learning app based in Canada is launching in Japan. It wants its service running close to Japanese learners right away, without building any facilities there. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud applies?

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.why: This benefit is about how the bill is shaped, while the need here is to reach a new country quickly.
Speed and agility covers fast experiments by teams, while the need here is a presence in another country.
Deploying into an existing AWS Region abroad, instead of building there, is the go global in minutes benefit.
Stop guessing capacity is about sizing resources to demand, while the need here is a location near learners.

questions.takeaway: A cost allocation tag must be activated before Cost Explorer can group spend by it.

read.text: AWS cost allocation tags come in two types, AWS-generated and user-defined, and you must activate each before it appears in Cost Explorer or on a cost allocation report.

questions.stem: A marketing agency labels each resource with a tag that names the client it serves, and it wants AWS Cost Explorer to show spend per client. What must the agency do before the tag shows up in Cost Explorer?

options.text: Activate the tag as a cost allocation tag
options.why: A user-defined tag appears in Cost Explorer only after it is activated as a cost allocation tag.

options.text: Create a budget in AWS Budgets filtered by the tag
options.why: A tag-filtered budget can warn about a client's spend, but it does not make the tag appear in Cost Explorer.

options.text: Link its accounts through consolidated billing
options.why: Consolidated billing merges accounts into one bill, but tags stay hidden from Cost Explorer until activated.

options.text: Model each client in the AWS Pricing Calculator
options.why: The Pricing Calculator estimates planned designs, so it has no effect on what Cost Explorer reports for running resources.
